title: You can shout all day…
paragraphs:
You can shout all day…
and still have no fire.

You can look spiritual…
and still be empty.
Because noise is not proof of God.
And Mount Carmel exposes something most of us don’t want to admit.

You can worship…
and still be wrong.

Elijah stood there—alone.
Dust on his skin.
Fire not yet fallen.
Silence still hanging in the air.

Cutting themselves.
Begging a god that could not answer.
And here’s the part that pierced me—
But sincerity doesn’t make something true.

You can be passionate and still be deceived.
You can be loud and still be lost.
You can be religious and still be far from God.
Some of us aren’t far from those prophets.

We don’t bow to Baal statues—
but we bow to approval.

We don’t build altars of stone—
but we build identities on success, image, control, secret habits no one sees.

We don’t cut ourselves with knives—
but we slowly bleed through comparison, insecurity, addiction, hidden sin.
We call it “just how life is.”
But heaven calls it something else.
“How long will you waver between two opinions? If the LORD is God, follow him; but if Baal is God, follow him.” (1 Kings 18:21)

How long will you keep living two lives?
One for Sunday.
One for the secret places.

How long will you say “I trust God” but panic when control slips?
How long will you lift your hands in worship… but refuse to surrender what’s hidden?
Some scholars interpret “waver” here as “limping” between two sides—like a man trying to walk in two directions at once.
That’s why your soul feels tired.
Because divided devotion will always drain you.
And here’s where it gets uncomfortable—
God did not answer the prophets of Baal.
But because Baal was never real.
And some of you are in a season of silence right now.

Prayers feel empty.
Worship feels dry.
You’re asking, “God, where are You?”
It’s not that God is silent.
It’s that something else has been sitting on the altar.
“He repaired the altar of the LORD that had been torn down.” (1 Kings 18:30)

We want the fire.
We want the breakthrough.
We want the power.
But we don’t want to deal with the broken altar.

The neglected prayer life.
The hidden compromise.
The quiet disobedience we keep excusing.
But heaven does not fall on divided altars.
And then Elijah does something shocking.
He pours water on the sacrifice.
Because when God moves, there will be no confusion who did it.

No manipulation.
No hype.
No emotional trick.
“Then the fire of the LORD fell and consumed the burnt offering, the wood, the stones and the soil, and also licked up the water in the trench.” (1 Kings 18:38)
God doesn’t just touch the surface.

The visible.
The hidden.
Even the soaked places you thought were beyond hope.
This is where shame meets redemption.

“My life is too messy.”
“My heart is too divided.”
“My past is too stained.”
But the fire of God doesn’t avoid broken altars.
It falls on them—when they are surrendered.
And this is where the story explodes into the Gospel.
At Carmel, the sacrifice was consumed by fire.
At the cross, Jesus became the sacrifice.
“For Christ also suffered once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, that he might bring us to God…” (1 Peter 3:18)

The fire you deserved for your sin…
fell on Him.

The judgment you should carry…
was placed on Jesus.
“There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.” (Romans 8:1)

Not reduced condemnation.
Not delayed condemnation.
That means your secret sin does not have the final word.
Your failure is not your identity.
Your shame is not your name.
But grace is not permission to stay divided.
Grace is the power to come home.
What is sitting on your altar right now?
What have you been protecting instead of surrendering?
What have you been feeding… that is starving your soul?
Because the same God who answered by fire—
Not always with flames from heaven.
A restored relationship with Him through Jesus Christ.
“If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” (1 John 1:9)
Call on the name of Jesus.
Let Him rebuild what you broke.
Let Him cleanse what you hid.
Let Him restore what you thought was lost.
